FINAL IVX IA REAL SENIOR DEVELOPER RECOVERY
200-ROOT FORENSIC AUDIT, FIX, QA, DEPLOY, AND VERIFY

EXECUTE NOW — DO NOT RETURN A PLAN
DO NOT RETURN GENERIC HEALTH TESTS
DO NOT RETURN “NO CODE CHANGE REQUIRED” WHEN THE REQUEST REQUIRES A FIX
DO NOT CREATE DUPLICATE JOBS
DO NOT CLAIM VERIFIED WITHOUT PRODUCTION EVIDENCE

==================================================
CONFIRMED CURRENT FAILURE
==================================================

The owner requested a real chat-module correction:

- Load the IVX chat faster.
- Open the most recently used conversation.
- Display the latest messages.
- Stop opening conversations from months ago.
- Audit chat logs.
- Fix, test, deploy, and verify live.

The system created worker task IDs, but the worker only ran:

- bun test
- curl /health

It did not:

- inspect the relevant chat source files;
- identify the conversation-ordering root cause;
- modify code;
- run chat-specific tests;
- run typecheck;
- commit a fix;
- deploy the fix;
- verify the behavior on the Android application.

This proves that the chat-to-worker connection exists, but the worker is still operating as a generic smoke-test worker instead of a complete senior developer executor.

==================================================
TARGET EXECUTION FLOW
==================================================

Owner request
→ Intent classification
→ Exactly one persistent job
→ Repository workspace created
→ Relevant files discovered
→ Root cause identified
→ Code modified
→ Targeted tests added
→ Typecheck completed
→ Full regression completed
→ Commit created
→ Push completed
→ Staging deployed
→ Device QA completed
→ Production deployed after authorization
→ Production behavior verified
→ Evidence returned in IVX IA Chat

==================================================
200 ROOTS TO AUDIT AND FIX
==================================================

PHASE 1 — REQUEST CLASSIFICATION AND ROUTING

ROOT 001 — Verify the owner’s message reaches the production IVX IA Chat API unchanged.

ROOT 002 — Preserve the complete owner prompt without summarizing away required actions.

ROOT 003 — Classify “audit,” “fix,” “test,” “deploy,” and “verify” as execution verbs.

ROOT 004 — Classify chat loading and message ordering as a code-development request.

ROOT 005 — Prevent this request from being routed as a general question.

ROOT 006 — Prevent this request from being routed as a generic health audit.

ROOT 007 — Prevent the legacy narrative model from answering before job creation.

ROOT 008 — Ensure both `self_developer` and `developer_executor` routes reach the worker.

ROOT 009 — Record the selected route in the job ledger.

ROOT 010 — Record the routing reason and confidence.

ROOT 011 — Reject route decisions that lose the requested module name.

ROOT 012 — Include “IVX chat module” in the normalized worker goal.

ROOT 013 — Include “most recent conversation first” in the acceptance criteria.

ROOT 014 — Include “latest messages visible after opening” in the acceptance criteria.

ROOT 015 — Include “loading performance” in the acceptance criteria.

ROOT 016 — Include “audit chat logs” in the execution scope.

ROOT 017 — Include “Android verification” in the execution scope.

ROOT 018 — Include “deployment” only when explicitly requested or owner-approved.

ROOT 019 — Do not reinterpret the request as “check whether the current app is healthy.”

ROOT 020 — Add a routing regression test using the exact owner prompt.

PHASE 2 — JOB CREATION AND DUPLICATE PREVENTION

ROOT 021 — Create exactly one job for one owner message.

ROOT 022 — Use the source message ID as an idempotency key.

ROOT 023 — Include the conversation ID in the idempotency key.

ROOT 024 — Include the owner ID in the idempotency key.

ROOT 025 — Store the idempotency key under a database uniqueness constraint.

ROOT 026 — Prevent two simultaneous POST requests from creating two job IDs.

ROOT 027 — Replace in-memory read-before-write checks with an atomic database claim.

ROOT 028 — Use an atomic insert, transaction, advisory lock, or unique-conflict return.

ROOT 029 — Make Retry reattach to the existing job.

ROOT 030 — Make a mobile double-tap return the existing task ID.

ROOT 031 — Persist the job before returning HTTP 202.

ROOT 032 — Return the task ID in under five seconds.

ROOT 033 — Store the original prompt exactly.

ROOT 034 — Store the normalized technical goal separately.

ROOT 035 — Store required outcomes separately from the goal.

ROOT 036 — Store requested deployment authorization.

ROOT 037 — Store the originating app build and platform.

ROOT 038 — Store the active GitHub repository and branch.

ROOT 039 — Store the assigned worker identity.

ROOT 040 — Add a test proving one message cannot create duplicate jobs.

ROOT 041 — Select a code-development worker, not a smoke-test-only worker.

ROOT 042 — Verify the selected worker has repository read access.

ROOT 043 — Verify the selected worker has repository write access.

ROOT 044 — Verify the selected worker can create a branch or isolated worktree.

ROOT 081 — Search for the conversation list query.

PHASE 6 — CONVERSATION ORDERING ROOT CAUSE

ROOT 101 — Determine whether conversations are ordered by creation date instead of recent activity.

ROOT 102 — Determine whether `updated_at` is not refreshed when a new message is sent.

ROOT 103 — Determine whether `last_message_at` is missing or null.

ROOT 104 — Determine whether null timestamps sort before valid timestamps.

ROOT 108 — Determine whether the first database row is selected regardless of activity.

ROOT 109 — Determine whether pagination returns an old page first.

ROOT 111 — Determine whether timezone conversion changes message order.

ROOT 113 — Determine whether a missing conversation participant row causes fallback selection.

ROOT 114 — Determine whether a legacy conversation table is mixed with the active table.

ROOT 116 — Determine whether messages are queried without an explicit `ORDER BY`.

ROOT 117 — Determine whether the UI expects newest-first while the API returns oldest-first.

ROOT 118 — Determine whether scrolling logic moves the user to an old message after loading.

ROOT 119 — Prove the exact root cause with query output and code evidence.

ROOT 120 — Record the exact file and line where incorrect ordering is introduced.

ROOT 121 — Measure initial conversation-list load time.

ROOT 122 — Measure selected-conversation message load time.

ROOT 123 — Measure time to first visible message.

ROOT 124 — Measure time to latest visible message.

ROOT 125 — Measure database query duration.

ROOT 128 — Check for N+1 participant or profile queries.

ROOT 132 — Check whether media metadata is loaded before text becomes visible.

ROOT 133 — Check whether large attachments block the first render.

ROOT 134 — Check whether message components perform expensive parsing repeatedly.

ROOT 135 — Check whether Realtime events trigger full history reloads.

ROOT 136 — Add indexes for actual chat ordering and lookup queries where required.

ROOT 137 — Add bounded pagination for conversation history.

ROOT 138 — Load recent messages first while retaining access to older history.

ROOT 139 — Add performance instrumentation with trace IDs.

ROOT 140 — Establish measurable loading acceptance thresholds.

PHASE 8 — IMPLEMENTATION REQUIREMENTS

ROOT 141 — Update the backend query to order conversations by verified recent activity.

ROOT 142 — Use a deterministic secondary sort key.

ROOT 143 — Update `last_message_at` atomically when a message is stored.

ROOT 144 — Backfill missing conversation activity timestamps safely if required.

ROOT 145 — Select the most recently active conversation on initial opening.

ROOT 146 — Respect the owner’s explicitly selected conversation during the same session.

ROOT 147 — Do not automatically restore a stale conversation from months ago.

ROOT 148 — Validate the stored conversation ID before restoring it.

ROOT 149 — Fall back to the most recent valid conversation when restoration fails.

ROOT 150 — Fetch the latest message page for the selected conversation.

ROOT 151 — Sort message records deterministically by server timestamp and stable ID.

ROOT 153 — Scroll to the latest message only after layout and data are ready.

ROOT 154 — Prevent old-page pagination from forcing the viewport away from the latest message.

ROOT 155 — Prevent duplicate messages from Realtime plus initial fetch.

ROOT 158 — Prevent state updates after component unmount.

ROOT 162 — Test opening the chat with one conversation.

ROOT 163 — Test opening the chat with many conversations.

ROOT 182 — Run chat integration tests.

ROOT 183 — Run API contract tests.

ROOT 184 — Run database query tests.

PHASE 11 — COMMIT, DEPLOYMENT, AND LIVE VERIFICATION

ROOT 195 — Deploy through the approved production pipeline.

ROOT 197 — Install or refresh the production Android application and repeat the owner scenario.

ROOT 200 — Return the complete proof ledger and mark VERIFIED only after every required gate passes.

==================================================
MANDATORY WORKER DECISION RULE
==================================================

For a request that explicitly requires a behavior change, the worker has only three valid outcomes:

A. FIXED
- Relevant files inspected
- Root cause proven
- Code changed
- Tests pass
- Commit created
- Deployment completed when authorized
- Production behavior verified

B. BLOCKED WITH SPECIFIC TECHNICAL EVIDENCE
- Exact missing permission, failed command, unavailable file, merge conflict, test failure, or production blocker
- File, command, status code, and error included
- No generic “no changes required” response

C. ALREADY CORRECT, PROVEN BY TARGETED REPRODUCTION
- The exact requested behavior is reproduced successfully
- Chat-specific tests prove it
- Production device verification proves it
- The owner’s screenshot is explained by a different confirmed cause

The following response is forbidden:

- “NO CODE CHANGED”
- generic `bun test`
- generic `/health 200`
- “the inspected target already satisfies the goal”

unless the exact owner-reported behavior was tested and proven correct.

==================================================

==================================================
